## 席位核对

**ACCEPT** · `domain:skills#1` · `session_01ADHkmSrRBdu9MdC6fc33Uu` · head `69484961` · 2026-10-27T18:20Z

1. 形态 — Tier H (`docs/adr/**`): new ADR-0143 (Proposed) moves outbound connector auth into the open tier — `oauth2` (`authorization_code` + S256 PKCE + refresh, `client_credentials`, the MCP authorization flow), `app-credential` (`feishu` / `dingtalk` / `wecom`), `signed` (closed scheme enum) — with per-dispatch resolution (D4), a connection record outside metadata (D3), a server-side Connect flow (D5) and "a grant is never a sign-in" (D6). Dated, append-only amendment notes on ADR-0015, -0018, -0022, -0023, -0024, -0097; README index regenerated. No spec, runtime or console change.
2. 前提实测 — on `origin/main` `0ea90c7a`: ADR-0097:119 "deliberately omits OAuth2 from `ConnectorInstanceAuthSchema`"; `connector-auth.zod.ts:158–163` unions none / bearer / api-key / basic; L113–114 still say "intentionally absent (enterprise tier, ADR-0015)" (wrapped — the claim's grep missed it, corrected in amendment 6449956947). ADR-0018:229 is the sixth enterprise placement; round 2 gave it a note.
3. 门禁 check-runs — dev ran the 21 derived commands on the head, all exit 0 (`--ran` 21/21, 0 NOT-MEASURED). `check:adr-symbol-anchors` refuses `file:line` in `docs/adr`, so the record cites `path#symbol`; the `file:line` readings are in the PR body. CI on the head is read again before landing.
4. 接受的偏差 — `Refs #26768` sits on body line 3, after the harness attribution block. The four maintainer decisions (Q1 connection ownership, Q2 grant storage, Q3 first products, Q4 first signing schemes) stay open with recommendations — answered by the maintainer in the file before the merge, never by the seat.
5. 范围外去向 — card item 3, the cloud-repository `## Provenance` record (Prime Directive 13): this lane cannot reach `objectstack-ai/cloud`; ADR-0143's Provenance section names it as owed; the seat routes it to the maintainer. Contract review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, effort ≥ `xhigh` (triage 6448154988): requested from the director seat.
6. 落地条款 — governed, Tier H: stays draft until a `GOVERNED_APPROVERS` approval with Q1–Q4 answered; then it lands through the queue. #26702 and #26710 leave `pm:blocked` after it lands.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `694849615009fa10029d77321d261fe5b60f8398`
Local-runs: none
Scope: docs/adr/0143-outbound-connector-auth-is-open-tier.md + docs/adr/0015-external-datasource-federation.md, docs/adr/0018-unified-node-action-registry.md, docs/adr/0022-connectors-vs-messaging-channels.md, docs/adr/0023-openapi-to-connector-generator.md, docs/adr/0024-mcp-connectors.md, docs/adr/0097-declarative-connector-instances.md, docs/adr/README.md, AGENTS.md, packages/spec/src/shared/connector-auth.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/integration/connector.zod.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/plugin.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/credential-resolver.ts, packages/connectors/connector-mcp/src/mcp-provider.ts, packages/connectors/connector-openapi/src/openapi-connector.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-account.object.ts, docs/adr/0073-automation-execution-identity.md

Director seat (summon #52, ledger objectstack#12708), summoned by the `domain:skills#1` seat; effort ≥ `xhigh` per triage 6448154988. Read-only at the head above: the diff, card #26768 and its thread (claim 6449307005, amendment 6449956947, dev report 6449922632), the seat's ACCEPT 6450167841, the parent cards #26702 and #26710 for the quoted rulings, every file the ADR cites on `origin/main` `0ea90c7a`, AGENTS.md Prime Directives #12–#14 and Route & surface ownership rule 5, the head's check runs. `docs/adr/**` is a governed-register row ⇒ the rules face, `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`; Tier H, lands by the maintainer's hand with Q1–Q4 answered, not on this record. Served at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. The seat records; it does not approve, ready, queue or merge.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The rulings are quoted verbatim and the record executes them, no more.** #26702's body carries 「OAuth 放开源层，先起草 ADR 修订」, 「平台基于 better-auth ，怎么会有没有 oauth」, 「创建issue 就行」; #26710's body carries 「三条行动建议 立卡」 → 「建议 1+2立卡」 → 「3 不考虑」 and says of itself "This card is recommendation 2", so "recommendation 2 is request signing" is read, not inferred. D1–D7 cover exactly the two cards' item 1; recommendation 3 is listed under "does not decide" (「3 不考虑」). The four maintainer decisions are left open with options and a recommendation each — the seat decided none of them.
- **Every current-state claim is true on `main`.** `connector-auth.zod.ts`: `ConnectorOAuth2Schema` inlines `clientSecret` (L35) and `refreshToken` (L38) and sits in the runtime union `ConnectorAuthConfigSchema` (L79–85), which is `ConnectorSchema.authentication` (`connector.zod.ts:864`); `ResolvedConnectorAuth` `Extract`s the four static kinds (L99–102) and its docblock still places OAuth2 in "the enterprise tier (ADR-0015)"; the "OAuth2 is intentionally / absent (enterprise tier, ADR-0015)" sentence wraps L113–114 exactly as the ADR says; `ConnectorInstanceAuthSchema` unions none / bearer / api-key / basic (L158–163). `DeclarativeConnectorEntrySchema` refuses any non-`none` `authentication` on every published entry (`connector.zod.ts:1178–1192`). `ConnectorOAuth2Schema` has no runtime consumer — only its own tests parse it (D7 holds). `resolveInstanceAuth` resolves once and switches on the three static secret kinds only (`plugin.ts:2306–2337`), picked at materialization (`:1955`, `:1997`). `applyAuthToHeaders` folds the four static kinds (`mcp-provider.ts:63–79`); `normalizeTransport` exists (`:83`). `OpenApiSecurityScheme` types `oauth2` and `securitySchemes` has one occurrence in the file — the declaration — so "typed, never read" is measured. `sys_account.user_id` is `required: true` (`sys-account.object.ts:183–187`); its token columns are `Field.textarea` + `internal: true`, not the `secret` channel (`:236–255`). The IMAP `MailCredentialProvider.credentialFor` seam and its "the provider's job, not the connector's" sentence are at `connector-imap/src/account.ts:60–69`. ADR-0073's 2026-07-28 amendment (user-less data ops refused) exists.
- **The attribution finding is right.** ADR-0015 on `main` contains neither "OAuth" nor "enterprise" (both counts 0); its §10 speaks of `credentialsRef` into a secrets service (L698–699). The five records that place OAuth2 refresh in the enterprise tier each do so "per ADR-0015": ADR-0018 L229 ("on the ADR-0015 precedent"), ADR-0022 L112, ADR-0023 L114, ADR-0024 L111, ADR-0097 L71 and L119. So the ADR-0015 note changes attribution only, and each other note sits under the paragraph it amends. ADR-0024's note is also right that the record "names no OAuth" (count 0) and that §3 L102 says "we do not model the upstream's auth in `ConnectorSchema`".
- **The notes are append-only, as Prime Directive #13 requires.** Every hunk on the six existing records is a pure insertion: one `**Amended by**:` header line (the ADR-0005 convention) and one dated blockquote (the ADR-0092 / ADR-0099 "Amendment note (…)" convention). No existing line changes. Each note names what moves and what keeps its placement (vault backend, catalogs, marketplace, sandboxed stdio, the `sys_channel_account` lifecycle), matching D1 word for word.
- **Provenance follows Prime Directive #13's shape.** The directive puts a commercial-boundary decision in `objectstack-ai/cloud` and has this repo carry the mechanism half with a `## Provenance` section. The six tier-placing records are all in this repository and none cites a cloud record, so the ADR correctly records that the cloud half is owed and that the cloud record decides the commercial boundary where they disagree. D5 cites Route & surface ownership rule 5 ("declares its CLOSED query-parameter set on the day it lands") — that rule exists with that wording. D2's "closed enum, refused at publish when unknown" is Prime Directive #12's reject-at-authoring rule, cited correctly.
- **The index is the generator's.** `docs/adr/README.md` moves 143 → 144 records, Proposed 17 → 18, one ADR-0143 row; 0143 is free on `main` (0142 the newest). `Lint · repo & tooling gates` (home of `check:adr-index`) and `Lint · docs & code guards` (home of `check:adr-symbol-anchors`) are green on the head, so the row and every `path#symbol` anchor resolve.

### ② Semver level

`skip-changeset`: docs/adr only, no package touched. Correct — an ADR publishes nothing. The slices it names each carry their own changeset when they land.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Governed path (`docs/adr/**`, Tier H): no review yet; draft; `requested_reviewers` hotlong, os-zhuang. This seat's account is not a `GOVERNED_APPROVERS` member; this record is not an approval and does not lift Tier H. Per its own Status line the maintainer's merge, with Q1–Q4 answered in the file, is the acceptance act — the seat may not answer them.
- **Should-fix before the merge (text, in the file the maintainer edits anyway):** the ADR's own count is inconsistent after round 2 added the ADR-0018 note. L5 says "The five amendment notes this record names land in the same PR" — there are six (ADR-0015, -0018, -0022, -0023, -0024, -0097; L17 itself says "All six carry a dated amendment note"). L36 says "the six records that put outbound OAuth2 in the enterprise tier — ADR-0018, -0022, -0023, -0024 and -0097" — that list is five, and ADR-0015 is not one of them by the ADR's own finding. Neither changes a decision; both would be quoted wrong by the next reader. The seat should push the two words before the maintainer's edit, or the maintainer fixes them in the same stroke as Q1–Q4.
- Check runs on `69484961` at this record: 22 `success` (every Lint job, `Check Documentation Links`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`), 16 expected skips (docs-only), `Test Core (1/8)` and `Type Check · workspace` still `in_progress`. Nothing red; a red re-opens this record.
- Card item 3 (the cloud-repository record with a `## Provenance` pointer back to ADR-0143) is not in this PR and cannot be: the lane has no reach into `objectstack-ai/cloud`. The ADR names it as owed; the seat routed it to the maintainer. That is the right disposition; it is also the one standing item Steve already has open from #26059's ruling (no seat here can file in cloud).
- Dev open questions (6449922632): channel accounts stay out (A) — right, the cards and rulings are about connectors and no channel transport is built; `app-credential` as its own discriminant (A) — right, the vendor exchanges are not RFC 6749 grants and folding them into `oauth2` would make one key mean two things; notes written in force though Proposed (A) — right, the Status line says the notes take effect with the merge that accepts the record, and a conditional note would be rewritten on that day anyway.
- Not owed a note: ADR-0023 L29's "managed OAuth2 refresh" sits in the Context comparison table (activepieces vs. us), a description of the other project, not a tier placement; the ADR's Amends list is right to leave it.
- Dev deviations: `path#symbol` in place of `file:line` (the symbol-anchor gate refuses line anchors in `docs/adr/**`; the line readings are in the PR body and re-measured here); `Refs #26768` on body line 3 after the harness attribution block; `main` moved past the base — nothing since touches `docs/adr/`'s six records or the index inputs beyond what the green index gate already proves.

### ④ Design judgment

- **The record as a contract**, against the code it will govern: D2's three variants are each closed where the code today is open-by-omission, and every secret stays a `credentialRef` — the one invariant `DeclarativeConnectorEntrySchema` already enforces is extended rather than relaxed. D3 keeps tokens out of `sys_metadata`, the discovery route and logs; D4 names the two failure classes with ADR-0097's own split (operational `CONNECTOR_UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE` on backoff vs. a revoked grant that degrades with a reason and never fails boot), which is the degrade-don't-die rule ADR-0097 §"Upstream availability" already landed. D6 is the right guard for the one thing Q2's option A would otherwise make easy: a connector grant becoming a sign-in row. The Q2 analysis is measured, not argued — three of D3/D6's requirements fail on `sys_account`'s actual columns (`user_id` required, tokens not on the `secret` channel, a row keyed as a linked sign-in), so the recommendation of a dedicated object follows from the file, not from taste. Q1's recommendation (organization-shared now, per-user additive later) is consistent with ADR-0073's user-less refusal and with `Metadata-protocol: added` being the cheaper later move. Q4's enum rule (a scheme enters with its signer and vendor vectors, ADR-0049) is the only honest shape for security-critical canonicalisation. Holds; nothing to break.
- **The amendment notes as amendments:** each reverses one row and names what stays, under the paragraph that drew the line, with the ADR-0015 note confined to attribution. That is the narrowest edit Prime Directive #13 allows and still leaves a future reader with the right pointer. Holds, with the two count words above corrected.
